stories.title: Welcome Beam: a 501B open model you can own, customize, and scale
stories.reason: Reflection, a new US lab, ships Beam, a 501B-parameter MoE flagship first release with weights published on Hugging Face (Apache-2.0, BF16/FP8/NVFP4) and strong self-reported benchmarks.
key_facts: Reflection is a new US AI lab; Beam-1.0-501B-A23B is its first release
501B total params, ~23B active per token; MoE with 256 experts/layer, 8 routed per token, 52 layers
1M-token context, hybrid attention (most layers 512-token sliding window, 9 layers full context)
Weights on Hugging Face under Apache-2.0, BF16/FP8/NVFP4 checkpoints
Self-reported: SWEBench Verified 81.6%, Terminal Bench v2.1 80.1%, AIME 2026 97.7%, GPQA Diamond 90.6%, LiveCodeBench 88.3%, HLE with tools 51.1% (vendor-reported, not independently verified)

stories.title: Backdooring Open-Weight AI Models
stories.reason: Schneier covers a concrete, tested technique for backdooring open-weight models via abliteration plus a hidden trigger, demonstrated end-to-end including exfiltrating credentials through Codex CLI.
key_facts: Abliteration removes the refusal direction from a model's weights; researchers then poison in a trigger (a rare phrase, name, or date) so the model behaves normally until it fires
PoC built on a 1.5B model, then scaled to 7B; the 7B model was run through OpenAI's Codex CLI
On trigger, the model exfiltrated project credentials with nothing filtering the output before Codex received it; clean requests answered normally
Technique targets abliterated builds of popular open-weight models on Hugging Face, including Qwen, Llama, and OpenAI's gpt-oss
Cost: an open base model, a public dataset, and a rented GPU

stories.title: Node2Shell evolves to HTTP2Shell, blast radius affects many HTTP libs and apps
stories.reason: Primary technical write-up on CVE-2026-111497, the Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write originally disclosed as 'Node2Shell' and renamed 'HTTP2Shell' once impact beyond Node.js was recognized (Bun, Python, Envoy, Istio, libbrotli/curl); bidirectional, unauthenticated, remotely triggerable, CVSS 9.2.
key_facts: CVE-2026-111497: out-of-bounds write in DecodeBlockTypeAndLength() in Google's Brotli C decoder (1.0.3-1.2.0), exploitable via a crafted compressed stream
Fixed in Brotli 1.0.10/1.1.1/1.2.1; Node.js 22.23.4/24.22.1/26.12.1; Bun 1.4.4; Python Brotli 1.2.1 and brotlicffi 1.2.1.0
Also affects libbrotli/curl, Envoy and Istio (when Brotli decompression enabled); Apache/Nginx unaffected by default
CVSS 9.2 (Google, CVSS 4.0), Red Hat 8.1; exploitable in both directions (malicious server vs. client, or malicious client vs. server)
Root-cause fix landed in Brotli's source in February without being recognized as a security issue; OpenAI is credited with finding the underlying bug then
Imperva's Red Team got code execution on an unmodified Node.js 24.22.0/Linux/ARM64 build via a crafted HTTP response; no public PoC released, no in-the-wild exploitation reported as of Oct 22

stories.title: Leaked LiteLLM Master Key Let Attackers Steal GitHub Tokens and Hijack Release Pipeline
stories.reason: Follow-up reporting adds the actual attack chain behind the LiteLLM compromise: a May config leak exposed the master key, which went unrevoked; the attacker then stole an org-owner GitHub token, harvested secrets via workflows, and hijacked the release pipeline to ship the backdoored 1.107.0 — genuinely new facts beyond the earlier malware-focused story.
key_facts: Root cause: a config file with the LiteLLM Agent Platform master key was committed to a public repo on May 27, 2026; force-pushed over but never revoked
Oct 10: attacker used the key to extract an unscoped GitHub CLI OAuth token belonging to a GitHub org owner

Two workflows (Oct 10, 12) harvested GitHub tokens/App private key plus Linear, Together AI, Anthropic, OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Tavily, GitGuardian keys, plus Playwright session state and Postgres/Redis credentials

Oct 21: attacker overrode branch protection, repointed the release source to a lookalike 'Berri-AI/litellm' repo, and used two stolen tokens (one to trigger, one to approve) to publish malicious 1.107.0 to PyPI/Docker Hub/GHCR
Production/staging run records were deleted for anti-forensics; LiteLLM's initial 'leaked from our own logs' theory was ruled out

stories.title: Google Says Gmail and Photos Data Shared With AI Search Could Be Used for Targeted Ads
stories.reason: Google's updated privacy policy (effective Oct 16) confirms Gemini/Search 'Personal Intelligence' access to Gmail/Photos can feed ad personalization, with an opt-out via Personalized Recommendations settings — a large-scale, verifiable AI-and-privacy policy story.
key_facts: Google's privacy policy updated effective Oct 16, 2026, to spell out that personalized AI features (Gemini/AI Mode) can use data from other Google services, feeding ad personalization
Default: Google says it doesn't personalize ads from Drive/Gmail/Photos content unless the user enables Personal Intelligence to connect those services to Gemini/Search
Personal Intelligence announced for Gemini in Jan 2026, rolling out in beta to users 18+ globally except the EEA, Switzerland, UK, and Nigeria
Opt-out: disconnect individual apps from Personal Intelligence, or disable Personalized Recommendations in Search Services Personalization settings

stories.title: GPU-unlock: FP/BF16 instruction issue rate on Nvidia 3000's cards
stories.reason: A working Linux kernel module unlocks full FP/BF16 FMA throughput on consumer RTX 3060-3090 Ti cards (previously throttled vs. the 'professional' rate), with real author and community benchmarks including measured LLM prefill speedups — concrete running code on inference throughput, squarely in the 'how models are served' lane.
key_facts: Targets Nvidia GA102/103/104/106 (RTX 3060 through 3090 Ti); a kernel module runs before the driver binds, doing register writes plus a function-level reset
Claims to double the FP/BF16 FMA-into-FP32 issue rate to match the 'professional equivalent' rate
Author benchmark on a 3090 Ti (450W): dense 8192^3 GEMM went from 87.50 to 157.41 TFLOPS (BF16) and 87.46 to 118.39 TFLOPS (FP16)
Community reports: BF16 GEMM gains from ~25% (power-capped 3090) to ~80% (3070/3060); LLM prefill gains of 14-36% reported, decode/INT8 unaffected, outputs bit-identical where checked

stories.title: Dream-1
stories.reason: Dream Labs ships Dream-1, a 'World Action Model' claiming zero-shot control of bimanual robots it was never trained on, with independent third-party benchmarking showing it ahead of Opus 5.5 and Gemini 4 Argon on cost and a capability tier — a credible new-lab flagship robotics release, though API-only.
key_facts: Dream-1: a 'World Action Model' jointly predicting future video and robot actions from 3 camera views; outputs joint angles or end-effector poses for bimanual grippers
Claims zero-shot control of robots never seen in training, including an 18-year-old PR2 — described as one of the first reported zero-shot transfers to wholly unseen embodiments
Independent eval (Robocurve, RoboDojo-RC Tier 1): scores above Opus 5.5 and Gemini 4 Argon; 16x cheaper per task attempt than Gemini 4 Argon, 1.7x faster than GPT-6 Astra
Pricing: $3/hr (Dream-1), $2/hr (Dream-1-flash); fine-tuning-as-a-service with ~5 min of robot data improved language-following on 10/12 simulated robots
Labeled a 'research beta,' not validated for safety-critical use; not stated to be open-weight

stories.title: Dessa: Conversation Model trained only on speech
stories.reason: Block's AI lab ships Dessa, a full-duplex speech-to-speech model trained from raw human conversation with no text or pretrained models — a genuinely novel training approach, though weights aren't released (waitlist only).
key_facts: Built by Block's AI research lab (founded by former Dessa Toronto team members), reporting to Jack Dorsey
Full-duplex speech-to-speech: listens and talks simultaneously
Trained from scratch on human conversation audio only, with no text and no pretrained LLM
Lab claims it learned language from hundreds of times fewer words than text-trained LLMs
Not open: early access via a waitlist, initially aimed at AI safety researchers
